statement: A jar holds 20 beads when it is full. There are 13 beads in it now. How many more beads fit in the jar?

choices.misconception: I counted 13, 14, and so on up to 20 and counted the 13 as well.
I gave how many beads are in the jar now.
I gave how many beads the jar holds when it is full.
I added 13 and 20 instead of finding the gap between them.

hints: Draw the full jar as one long bar.
The full jar is the whole. The beads already in it are one part, and the beads that still fit are the other part. Find the missing part.
Count up from 13 to 20 in steps, counting only the steps: 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20.

solutions.reliable: The full jar holds 20 and 13 are already in it, so 20 - 13 = 7 more fit. Check: 13 + 7 = 20. The idea to keep: whole minus the part you have gives the part that is missing.

whyOnTest: Finding a missing part from the whole is the core bar model, and counting the starting number is a common slip.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
